name: Metal Backend
description: The Metal RenderBackend: a device and its command queue, capability state behind one lock that no GPU wait holds (fail; recover, which clears a failure only after the health probe passes on a new queue; a health probe that runs one kernel from its own memo; recordCompletion, which marks the backend unhealthy on any command-buffer error; a failed texture allocation also marks it unhealthy), tiled rgba16Float surfaces (one texture per 256 px tile, shared storage on unified memory and managed on a discrete GPU) uploaded from Float32 pixel buffers through HalfFloat with every component clamped to the finite half range and downloaded back, tile eviction under a memory budget (budgetBytes, half the device's recommended working set by default: the least recently used tiles move to a CPU shadow until residentBytes fits, and a read merges resident tiles with shadows), and the pipeline cache: MSL compiled at runtime from string constants, once per PipelineKey (variants from outside go through PipelineKey.validated), memoised in process with Metal's own shader cache across launches; cacheURL is reserved and nothing is read, written or deleted there. Display encode (MB-3, enabled at init) runs the display_encode kernel over resident tiles, reading DisplayTable's thresholds and P3 matrix, and encodes evicted tiles from their shadows on the CPU. Transform (MB-7) runs on the GPU: crop as blit copies and quarter turns as a rotate kernel, piece by piece from TileMap into a new surface (an evicted source tile is copied from its shadow through a temporary texture), with the CPU backend's errors for an invalid crop. Normal composite (MB-4, enabled at init on a read-write tier 2 device only) runs the composite_normal kernel in place on the backdrop's tiles, piece by piece from CompositeMap, with CoreRaster's sourceOver rule, opacity check and clip (an evicted backdrop tile is brought back to a texture first and the budget enforced after; a source that is the backdrop is read from a snapshot). The eleven other separable modes (MB-5) run as variants of the same in-place path, one blendSeparable_<mode> kernel each with CoreRaster's blend formula, once .blendSeparable is enabled (MB-6 enables it at init; until then only the parity hook does, on read-write tier 2); non-separable modes throw unsupported. Resample (MB-8) runs bilinear and lanczos3 on the GPU as two separable passes of ResampleTable over whole-image float4 buffers in the CPU's pass order (the source read like `read`, resident tiles merged with shadows, and uploaded from the CPU), scattered into a new surface with components clamped to the finite half range; an invalid size throws the CPU backend's error. Adjust (MB-13) runs exposure, levels and curves through the adjust_tone kernel tile by tile into a new surface, reading AdjustTable's factor or table on unpremultiplied values with CoreRaster's alpha guard (an evicted source tile through a temporary texture) and the CPU backend's errors for invalid parameters; .adjust stays out of supports until MB-14. Every other op throws unsupported until its slice lands (non-separable blends MB-9 and MB-10, blur MB-11 and MB-12, white balance, contrast and highlights/shadows MB-14, retouch MB-15).
